entities.name: Ceolwulf I of Mercia
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Ceolwulf I of Mercia was the King of Mercia, a kingdom of Anglo-Saxon England, from 821 until his deposition in 823. He was the brother of Coenwulf, his predecessor, and was deposed by Beornwulf.

Ceolwulf I ascended to the throne following the death of his brother Coenwulf in 821, becoming the King of Mercia and ruling for two years until his deposition by his nephew Beornwulf in 823.

Ceolwulf I's reign was marked by the expansion of Mercia's borders, the strengthening of its economy, and the promotion of Christianity. He also oversaw the construction of several churches and monasteries throughout the kingdom.

Ceolwulf I's legacy is significant in the context of Anglo-Saxon England, as he played a key role in shaping the kingdom's politics, economy, and culture. His reign marked the beginning of a period of stability and growth for Mercia, which would last for several decades.

Ceolwulf I's story is one of the lesser-known yet fascinating stories of the Anglo-Saxon period, a time of great transformation and upheaval in Western Europe. His life and reign offer valuable insights into the politics, culture, and society of this pivotal moment in history.
